verdict.rationale: LocalAI ships a first-party natural-language agent, `local-ai chat`, which runs in the user's shell, reads files and runs commands on the machine behind an approval gate. In principle that lets a user drive LocalAI's own CLI by describing tasks in plain language. However, the evidence never shows the agent being used to administer LocalAI itself, such as installing models, configuring backends or managing nodes, so operating the product this way is only implied. Missing for 10: documented natural-language control of LocalAI's own management functions (model install, config, users, nodes), examples of the product operated via NL commands, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: local-ai chat reads your files and runs commands on your machine, behind an approval gate you control.
`local-ai chat`, an agent in your shell that runs commands behind an approval gate.
It answers questions, reads your files and runs commands on your machine, asking you to approve anything that changes state.
